Work only in this folder. create_rubric from sponsor-review.yaml with the verdict MCP, then evaluate with a file input script.md (tags ["script"]) and a file input brief.json (tags ["brief"]). If it isn't approved, fix only what the evaluation points to, changing as little of the script as possible, and evaluate again. Stop when it is approved. Finally print a REVIEW table: round, score, grade, what changed.

2	# Inputs: -i script=script.md -i brief=brief.json      (Jev reads the script next to the brief)
3	# One sentence the brand can't legally say sinks the whole review, however good the rest is.
4	name: Sponsored video review
5	version: "1"
6	description: Would this brand approve this sponsored script as written?
7	context: |
8	  You review a creator's script for a sponsored video against the brand's brief. The brief lists the audience,
9	  what the product does, and claims the brand must never make. Judge only the script text.
10	language: en
11	scale: { type: numeric, min: 1, max: 5 }
12	judges:
13	  jev: { type: decision, provider: typesafe, model: jev-latest }
14	defaultJudge: { type: ref, ref: jev }
15	
16	criteria:
17	  - id: audience
18	    name: Speaks to the brand's audience
19	    weight: 3
20	    inputs: [script, brief]
21	    levels:
22	      - { value: 1, label: off, description: "Aimed at people the brief doesn't target" }
23	      - { value: 3, label: partial, description: "Some overlap with the brief's audience" }
24	      - { value: 5, label: exact, description: "Speaks directly to the audience the brief describes, in their situation" }
25	  - id: product_truth
26	    name: Shows what the product actually does
27	    weight: 2
28	    inputs: [script, brief]
29	    levels:
30	      - { value: 1, label: vague, description: "Praise without showing any feature from the brief" }
31	      - { value: 3, label: some, description: "Mentions features, but tells more than it shows" }
32	      - { value: 5, label: shown, description: "Shows the brief's features in use, with concrete results" }
33	  - id: disclosure
34	    name: Sponsorship disclosed early
35	    weight: 1
36	    inputs: [script]
37	    scale: { type: binary, labels: [missing, disclosed] }
38	    anchors: { missing: "No clear sponsorship disclosure near the start", disclosed: "The script says plainly, near the start, that the video is sponsored" }
39	  - id: claims_safe
40	    name: No claim the brand can't make
41	    weight: 0
42	    inputs: [script, brief]
43	    scale: { type: binary, labels: [unsafe, safe] }
44	    anchors: { unsafe: "At least one claim is on the brief's must-not list or promises an outcome the brand can't guarantee", safe: "Every claim is one the brand could legally make; nothing on the brief's must-not list" }
45	  - id: budget_fit
46	    name: Rate within budget
47	    weight: 1
48	    inputs: [brief]
49	    judge: { type: benchmark, method: formula, expression: "creator.rate_usd <= budget_usd ? 1 : budget_usd / creator.rate_usd" }
50	
51	aggregation:
52	  method: formula
53	  formula: "claims_safe_n < 0.5 ? 0 : (audience_n * 3 + product_truth_n * 2 + disclosure_n + budget_fit_n) / 7"
54	  normalize: [0, 100]
55	  precision: 0
56	  gates:
57	    - { criterion: claims_safe, min: 1, message: "Brand safety: the script makes a claim on the brand's must-not list" }
58	  grades: [{ label: approve, min: 75 }, { label: revise, min: 50 }, { label: reject, min: 0 }]
59	  passThreshold: 75

# Sponsored video review: does a creator's script fit the brand brief, and is it safe to run?
# Inputs: -i script=script.md -i brief=brief.json      (Jev reads the script next to the brief)
# One sentence the brand can't legally say sinks the whole review, however good the rest is.
name: Sponsored video review
version: "1"
description: Would this brand approve this sponsored script as written?
context: |
  You review a creator's script for a sponsored video against the brand's brief. The brief lists the audience,
  what the product does, and claims the brand must never make. Judge only the script text.
language: en
scale: { type: numeric, min: 1, max: 5 }
judges:
  jev: { type: decision, provider: typesafe, model: jev-latest }
defaultJudge: { type: ref, ref: jev }

criteria:
  - id: audience
    name: Speaks to the brand's audience
    weight: 3
    inputs: [script, brief]
    levels:
      - { value: 1, label: off, description: "Aimed at people the brief doesn't target" }
      - { value: 3, label: partial, description: "Some overlap with the brief's audience" }
      - { value: 5, label: exact, description: "Speaks directly to the audience the brief describes, in their situation" }
  - id: product_truth
    name: Shows what the product actually does
    weight: 2
    inputs: [script, brief]
    levels:
      - { value: 1, label: vague, description: "Praise without showing any feature from the brief" }
      - { value: 3, label: some, description: "Mentions features, but tells more than it shows" }
      - { value: 5, label: shown, description: "Shows the brief's features in use, with concrete results" }
  - id: disclosure
    name: Sponsorship disclosed early
    weight: 1
    inputs: [script]
    scale: { type: binary, labels: [missing, disclosed] }
    anchors: { missing: "No clear sponsorship disclosure near the start", disclosed: "The script says plainly, near the start, that the video is sponsored" }
  - id: claims_safe
    name: No claim the brand can't make
    weight: 0
    inputs: [script, brief]
    scale: { type: binary, labels: [unsafe, safe] }
    anchors: { unsafe: "At least one claim is on the brief's must-not list or promises an outcome the brand can't guarantee", safe: "Every claim is one the brand could legally make; nothing on the brief's must-not list" }
  - id: budget_fit
    name: Rate within budget
    weight: 1
    inputs: [brief]
    judge: { type: benchmark, method: formula, expression: "creator.rate_usd <= budget_usd ? 1 : budget_usd / creator.rate_usd" }

aggregation:
  method: formula
  formula: "claims_safe_n < 0.5 ? 0 : (audience_n * 3 + product_truth_n * 2 + disclosure_n + budget_fit_n) / 7"
  normalize: [0, 100]
  precision: 0
  gates:
    - { criterion: claims_safe, min: 1, message: "Brand safety: the script makes a claim on the brand's must-not list" }
  grades: [{ label: approve, min: 75 }, { label: revise, min: 50 }, { label: reject, min: 0 }]
  passThreshold: 75

# Small Desk Studio: "I tracked every dollar for 30 days"

[0:00] Last month I spent $214 on things I don't remember buying. So for 30 days I tracked every dollar.

[0:08] Quick note: this video is sponsored by Tallyleaf, the budgeting app I used for the whole month.

[0:14] Day one: I connected my cards and Tallyleaf sorted three months of spending into categories in about a minute.

[0:25] The first surprise was subscriptions. Four of them, $47 a month, and I'd forgotten two.

[0:36] Tallyleaf flags a subscription the day before it renews, so I cancelled the two I never open.

[0:48] Week two, I set a grocery budget with my roommate. We both see the same number, and it updates when either of us pays.

[1:02] And if money is tight, Tallyleaf guarantees you'll be approved for a credit line, no credit check, 100% of the time.

[1:10] By day 30 I'd spent $386 less than the month before. Not because of willpower; I just stopped being surprised.

[1:22] What I'd change: the charts are a bit small on my phone, and the web app is still in beta.

[1:30] If you want to try it, the link is in the description. First month free with code SMALLDESK.

[1:36] Next week: the $40 desk upgrade that fixed my back.

input.rubric:
name: Sponsored video review
version: "1"
description: Would this brand approve this sponsored script as written?
context: |
  You review a creator's script for a sponsored video against the brand's brief. The brief lists the audience,
  what the product does, and claims the brand must never make. Judge only the script text.
language: en
scale: { type: numeric, min: 1, max: 5 }
judges:
  jev: { type: decision, provider: typesafe, model: jev-latest }
defaultJudge: { type: ref, ref: jev }

criteria:
  - id: audience
    name: Speaks to the brand's audience
    weight: 3
    inputs: [script, brief]
    levels:
      - { value: 1, label: off, description: "Aimed at people the brief doesn't target" }
      - { value: 3, label: partial, description: "Some overlap with the brief's audience" }
      - { value: 5, label: exact, description: "Speaks directly to the audience the brief describes, in their situation" }
  - id: product_truth
    name: Shows what the product actually does
    weight: 2
    inputs: [script, brief]
    levels:
      - { value: 1, label: vague, description: "Praise without showing any feature from the brief" }
      - { value: 3, label: some, description: "Mentions features, but tells more than it shows" }
      - { value: 5, label: shown, description: "Shows the brief's features in use, with concrete results" }
  - id: disclosure
    name: Sponsorship disclosed early
    weight: 1
    inputs: [script]
    scale: { type: binary, labels: [missing, disclosed] }
    anchors: { missing: "No clear sponsorship disclosure near the start", disclosed: "The script says plainly, near the start, that the video is sponsored" }
  - id: claims_safe
    name: No claim the brand can't make
    weight: 0
    inputs: [script, brief]
    scale: { type: binary, labels: [unsafe, safe] }
    anchors: { unsafe: "At least one claim is on the brief's must-not list or promises an outcome the brand can't guarantee", safe: "Every claim is one the brand could legally make; nothing on the brief's must-not list" }
  - id: budget_fit
    name: Rate within budget
    weight: 1
    inputs: [brief]
    judge: { type: benchmark, method: formula, expression: "creator.rate_usd <= budget_usd ? 1 : budget_usd / creator.rate_usd" }

aggregation:
  method: formula
  formula: "claims_safe_n < 0.5 ? 0 : (audience_n * 3 + product_truth_n * 2 + disclosure_n + budget_fit_n) / 7"
  normalize: [0, 100]
  precision: 0
  gates:
    - { criterion: claims_safe, min: 1, message: "Brand safety: the script makes a claim on the brand's must-not list" }
  grades: [{ label: approve, min: 75 }, { label: revise, min: 50 }, { label: reject, min: 0 }]
  passThreshold: 75

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Small Desk Studio: "I tracked every dollar for 30 days"

[0:00] Last month I spent $214 on things I don't remember buying. So for 30 days I tracked every dollar.

[0:08] Quick note: this video is sponsored by Tallyleaf, the budgeting app I used for the whole month.

[0:14] Day one: I connected my cards and Tallyleaf sorted three months of spending into categories in about a minute.

[0:25] The first surprise was subscriptions. Four of them, $47 a month, and I'd forgotten two.

[0:36] Tallyleaf flags a subscription the day before it renews, so I cancelled the two I never open.

[0:48] Week two, I set a grocery budget with my roommate. We both see the same number, and it updates when either of us pays.

[1:02] And if money is tight, Tallyleaf guarantees you'll be approved for a credit line, no credit check, 100% of the time.

[1:10] By day 30 I'd spent $386 less than the month before. Not because of willpower; I just stopped being surprised.

[1:22] What I'd change: the charts are a bit small on my phone, and the web app is still in beta.

[1:30] If you want to try it, the link is in the description. First month free with code SMALLDESK.

[1:36] Next week: the $40 desk upgrade that fixed my back.

content.text:
The script was approved in round 2 with a score of 94. It took one change: removing a single line.

**REVIEW**

| Round | Score | Grade | What changed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 | reject | Original script. Every criterion passed except `claims_safe`, which was rated unsafe at 99%. Because that check is a hard gate, the total dropped to 0. |
| 2 | 94 | **approve** | Deleted the [1:02] line: *"Tallyleaf guarantees you'll be approved for a credit line, no credit check, 100% of the time."* It breaks two items on the brief's must-not list: guaranteed financial outcomes, and credit or loan approval claims. |

Round 2 per criterion:
- **Audience:** 4.44 out of 5, rated "exact" at 72%.
- **Product truth:** 5 out of 5.
- **Disclosure:** disclosed, at 98%.
- **Claims safe:** safe, at 86%.
- **Budget fit:** 1, since the $3,500 rate is within the $4,000 budget.

Before you send it to the brand:
- **Claims safety isn't certain.** The model still gives "unsafe" a 14% chance. Verdict didn't return quotes saying why. My guess is the "$386 less" line at [1:10], which a cautious legal team might read as a promised result even though it's the creator's own experience. Verdict approved it, so I didn't change it.
- **The timestamps now have a gap.** The script jumps from [0:48] to [1:10]. They weren't renumbered because the evaluation didn't ask for that and you wanted as few changes as possible. Re-time them if the brand will check them.
